name: Track which brands AI answers name in your category with DataForSEO, OpenAI and Gmail

parameters.content:
## Who do the models name in your category

Every week: ask which brands come out of an assistant's mouth when it answers questions about your category, where you sit in that list, and which pages it quotes instead of yours. Then say what moved since last week.

### How it works

**`Ask Who The Models Name`** returns a ranked leaderboard of brands mentioned across captured AI answers - not one model's answer to one prompt, an aggregate over thousands. For `email marketing software` that was 1,383 brands.

Share of voice is measured against `aggregated_metrics.total.mentions`, the whole set, not against the 25 rows on screen. The leader in that test held 33 mentions out of 1,838, so a share computed over the visible rows would have been roughly ten times too flattering.

**`Read The Leaderboard`** drops category labels before ranking. The API mixes them with brands: positions 3, 7 and 10 were `CRM software company`, `CRM platform` and `technology company`. Your own brand is never dropped.

**`Ask Which Pages Get Quoted`** returns the URLs the answers cite, which is the part you can act on - a competitor page that keeps getting quoted is a page to answer.

Noise is controlled with a **domain** list, not keywords. Excluding a keyword changed nothing in testing; excluding a domain removed 1,550 mentions.

### Setup

1. A DataForSEO account, as an n8n **Basic Auth** credential - login is your email, password is the API password.

2. **Settings** takes your topics, your brand and domain, the platforms, the location and the addresses.

3. A Google Sheet with a tab called `history` and the header row `checked_on`, `topic_key`, `topic`, `platform`, `brand_rank`, `brand_mentions`, `share_pct`, `leader`, `leader_mentions`. It is append-only, so it is also the chart.

4. A Google Sheets credential, an OpenAI credential and a Gmail credential.

## 1. What to ask about
Topics are categories, not brand names. The question is who gets named when somebody asks about the category.

## 2. Two questions, side by side
Who gets named, and which pages the answers quote. Neither call needs the other, so neither waits. `chat_gpt` holds United States and English only.

## 3. Wait for all three
The history read runs beside both calls. Merge is the barrier that lets the next node reach back to all of them by name.

## 4. Remember, then compare
The snapshot is written every week whatever happened, so next week's comparison always spans exactly one week.

## 5. One email, only when there is data
A topic nobody asks an assistant about returns nothing. That ends quietly instead of mailing an empty table.

## This one costs money per run

Both DataForSEO calls are $0.10 per request plus $0.001 per row. Two topics on one platform at 25 rows is about $0.45 a week. Every topic you add is two more requests.

parameters.text:
=You are writing the weekly AI-visibility note for {{ $('Settings').first().json.brand }}.

Each row is one category topic on one AI platform. brand_rank is the brand's
position among real brands named in captured AI answers; 0 means it was not
named at all. share_pct is its share of every mention captured for that topic.
quoted_pages are the URLs those answers cite.

{{ JSON.stringify($json.rows, null, 1) }}

What moved since last week: {{ JSON.stringify($json.movers) }}

Write at most six bullets, plain text, no headings and no preamble.
Lead with the topic where the position changed most. Name the brand that
leads each topic and by how much. Where a cited page belongs to a competitor
and covers the topic, say which page and what it answers.
If the brand is unranked on a topic, say so plainly rather than softening it.
Never invent a number that is not in the data.
